quests.title: Penny Path Pocket Compass Route
quests.waitingUse: A quiet table-page activity where an adult reads the compass choices and the child writes a tiny errand route with one pencil.
quests.kidDirection: Fill the compass blanks to show where the button compass points and why the helper follows it.
quests.adultNote: Read the headings aloud, then let the child choose one snack-stand or mailbox detail before writing.

pageSections.heading: Compass Shop Start
lines: The button compass points first toward ____________________.
The folded receipt asks the helper to find ____________________.
The quiet clue near the snack stand is ____________________.

pageSections.heading: Kind Turn Map
lines: The compass changes direction after ____________________.
The mailbox row color I choose is ____________________.

pageSections.heading: Finish The Errand
lines: The helper solves the tiny errand by ____________________.
A clearer direction word I can add is ____________________.
My final Penny Path sentence is ____________________.

quests.takeHomeLine: Save this compass route page to finish a longer Penny Path errand story later.

quests.title: Margin Note Market Quiet Swap
quests.waitingUse: A quiet lobby activity where an adult points to three note choices and the child turns each one into a useful revision task.
quests.kidDirection: Turn three vague notes into specific revision tasks for a market stall writer.
quests.adultNote: If the wait is short, ask the child to finish only the strongest note and save the rest.

pageSections.heading: Market Stall Notes
lines: The Clarity stall receives a note that says ____________________.
The Detail stall needs one exact example about ____________________.
The Ending stall asks the writer to check ____________________.

pageSections.heading: Make Feedback Useful
lines: A vague note I can replace is ____________________.
My specific revision task says ____________________.
The writer should try this first because ____________________.

pageSections.heading: Next Draft Plan
lines: The market stall I would visit next is ____________________.
One sentence that needs a stronger detail is ____________________.
The calm note I would hand back says ____________________.

quests.takeHomeLine: Save this market page to finish the remaining note swaps at home or during another quiet wait.

quests.title: Clue Label Tower Gate Gallery
quests.waitingUse: A quiet gate-seat activity where an adult sets one printed page on a folder and the child writes exhibit labels from everyday-object clues.
quests.kidDirection: Choose three exhibit objects and write one clear label that tells visitors what to notice.
quests.adultNote: Invite the child to use nearby safe objects as inspiration while staying seated.

pageSections.heading: Gallery Object Picks
lines: The first exhibit object is ____________________.
The clue visitors should notice is ____________________.
A distracting detail I will leave out is ____________________.

pageSections.heading: One-Sentence Labels
lines: Label one should explain ____________________.
Label two should point visitors toward ____________________.
Label three becomes clearer when I add ____________________.

pageSections.heading: Curator Finish
lines: The label drawer I would open next is ____________________.
The clearest museum word on my page is ____________________.
My final exhibit label says ____________________.

quests.takeHomeLine: Save this gallery page so the final exhibit label can become a short museum story.

quests.title: Index Card Theater Seat-Row Cues
quests.waitingUse: A quiet adult-guided sibling activity where children stay seated, point to cue choices, and write stage-card lines on one page.
quests.kidDirection: Arrange the beginning, turn, and finish cues, then write the narrator's quiet closing line.
quests.adultNote: Give each child a turn choosing a cue, then keep the finished page in the folder if the wait ends.

pageSections.heading: Scene Card Row
lines: The beginning card shows ____________________.
The turn card changes the scene when ____________________.
The finish card should leave the audience noticing ____________________.

pageSections.heading: Quiet Cue Choices
lines: The action cue tells the actor to ____________________.
The dialogue cue line is ____________________.
The setting cue adds ____________________ to the tiny stage.

pageSections.heading: Closing Line
lines: The narrator reminds us that ____________________.
One jumpy part I can connect is ____________________.
My final seat-row cue says ____________________.

quests.takeHomeLine: Save this theater cue page to finish the scene-card performance plan later.
